entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail apprehending to his arrest relating to FIR/Crime No.1159/2023 dated 20-03-2023 registered at Police Station , Waidhan District Singrauli for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

2. It is contended by the counsel for the applicant that as per allegations levelled by the prosecution,
it is apparent that the present applicant has been made an accused alleging his involvement in preparation of a forged death certificate of Bansilal Mallah.

It is further contended by the counsel that in the present case, no case is made out against the applicant inasmuch as, the applicant did not play any role so far as the execution of sale deed is concerned.
It is further contended by the counsel that there are no allegation that the present applicant was instrumental in preparing forged death certificate of Bansilal Mallah.

It is also contended by the counsel that none of the ingredients of Arun Kumar Vishvakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191420930/
1 Sections 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC are made out against the applicant as there was no forgery which could have been attributed to the applicant and resultantly, as there was no forgery, there was no question of an offence of cheating in terms of Section 420 of IPC.

Thus, counsel submits that in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 as well as Sheila Sebastian vs. R. Jawaharaj and Another reported in (2018) 7 SCC 581, the present applicant deserves to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
3.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and submits that the present applicant is the person who persuaded the complainant to enter into sale deed and therefore, taking into consideration the active role played by the present applicant, the applicant's case is stand on a different footing then the case of co-accused Gulab Prasad Jaiswal,
who has been enlarged on anticipatory bail by this Court.
It is contended by the counsel that in the present case as per the allegations levelled against the present applicant, he is not entitled to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

4. Having considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the parties, prima facie, a perusal of the statements of complainant Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal and also his wife Smt. Rajkumari Jaiswal reveal that one Sitaram Vishwakarma had introduced his nephew to the complainant and had assured that the disputed property could have been purchased at a very reasonable rate and thereafter, the present applicant along with the then Patwari, took the complainant to the site and shown the land in question and after that, a sale deed was executed.

5. Therefore, taking into consideration the statements of complainant Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal and his wife Smt. Rajkumari Jaiswal as there are direct allegations against the present applicant, this Court is not inclined to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail as his case dose not stand on the similar footing with the case of co-accused Gulab Prasad Jaiswal.
6. Accordingly, this application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. stands dismissed.
